The '''Copa Paraguay''' is a knockout football competition in men's domestic Paraguayan [[association football|football]], starting in 2018 and succeeding the defunct [[Torneo República]]. The project for its creation was officially presented in December 2017 and approved by the [[Paraguayan Football Association]]'s Executive Committee on 20 February 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://objetivo.com.py/index.php/2018/02/21/copa-paraguay-abril/|title=Copa Paraguay, en abril|publisher=objetivo.com.py|date=20 February 2018|access-date=15 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190515063412/http://objetivo.com.py/index.php/2018/02/21/copa-paraguay-abril/|archive-date=15 May 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The competition starts in April and ends in November, with the winner of the cup qualifying for the following year's [[Copa Libertadores]] ([[Copa Sudamericana]] until the [[2022 Copa Paraguay|2022]] edition).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://versus.lanacion.com.py/versus/2022/12/22/es-oficial-el-campeon-de-la-copa-paraguay-ira-a-la-libertadores/|title=¡Es oficial! El campeón de la Copa Paraguay irá a la Libertadores|trans-title=It's official! The Copa Paraguay champion will go to the Libertadores|publisher=Versus|language=es|date=22 December 2022|access-date=22 January 2023}}</ref> If the cup winner has already qualified for South American competitions through the league, then the cup runner-up (or the third-placed team) will qualify. If the top three teams have all already qualified for South American competitions through the league, then the best-placed team in the [[Paraguayan Primera División]] that has not yet qualified for an international competition will qualify for the Copa Libertadores.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://d10.paraguay.com/la-copa-paraguay-otorgara-un-cupo-directo-la-sudamericana-n644024|title=La Copa Paraguay otorgará un cupo directo a la Sudamericana|publisher=d10.paraguay.com|date=9 February 2018}}</ref>

Starting from the [[2021 Copa Paraguay|2021 edition]], the winner also qualifies for the [[Supercopa Paraguay]].

==Format==
For its first edition in [[2018 Copa Paraguay|2018]], the competition was divided into two stages: a preliminary stage and the national stage.

In the preliminary stage, teams from the [[Paraguayan Primera División B|Primera B]], [[Paraguayan Cuarta División#Primera División C|Primera C]], and the [[Unión del Fútbol del Interior|UFI]] competed for 20 berths to the national stage: 7 Primera B teams, 6 from the Primera C, and 7 from the UFI qualified for the next stage of the competition.

In the national stage, the 12 [[Paraguayan Primera División|Primera División]] teams and the 16 [[Paraguayan División Intermedia|División Intermedia]] teams entered the competition, for a total of 48 teams which were drawn into 24 ties, with the winners qualifying for the second round. The 12 second round winners as well as the four best losers advanced to the round of 16. From that point onwards, the Copa Paraguay continued as a single-elimination tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.extra.com.py/deportes/la-copa-paraguay-ya-tiene-formato.html|title=La Copa Paraguay ya tiene formato|publisher=extra.com.py|date=24 December 2017}}</ref>

However, starting from [[2019 Copa Paraguay|the following edition]], the competition was expanded from 48 to 64 teams, allowing for greater participation from teams from the lower tiers and scrapping the preliminary round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoy.com.py/deportes/mas-equipos-en-copa-paraguay-para-el-2019|title=Más equipos en Copa Paraguay para el 2019|publisher=HOY|date=11 August 2018|access-date=19 May 2019}}</ref> It continued being a single-elimination tournament, with all teams entering the competition in the first stage. In April 2022, APF confirmed that a total of 74 teams would join the 2022 edition.<ref>[https://www.abc.com.py/deportes/futbol/2022/04/22/copa-paraguay-como-sera-el-nuevo-formato/|Copa Paraguay: ¿Cómo será el nuevo formato?]</ref>
